objects.definition:
typedef enum VSCMsgType {
    VSC_Init = 1,
    VSC_Error,
    VSC_ReaderAdd,
    VSC_ReaderRemove,
    VSC_ATR,
    VSC_CardRemove,
    VSC_APDU,
    VSC_Flush,
    VSC_FlushComplete
} VSCMsgType;
objects.description: Enumeration of all protocol message kinds exchanged between host and client in the Virtual Smart Card protocol.
Enumeration of error/result codes carried by VSCMsgError messages. Values indicate success or specific failure conditions.

Common header that prefixes every protocol message. 'type' is a VSCMsgType. 'reader_id' selects a reader (if applicable). 'length' is the payload size that follows immediately. 'data' is a zero-length array placeholder for the payload bytes.

Initialization/handshake payload exchanged once by both sides. Contains a magic constant, protocol version, and a variable-length capabilities array (at least one 32-bit entry; actual length inferred from header length).
Error/Status reply payload. 'code' is a VSCErrorCode reporting success or a specific error for prior requests.
Payload for announcing a new reader from client to host. Contains a variable-length UTF-8 name string bytes following the struct (length provided by header).
Empty payload indicating a reader has been removed on the client side.
Payload carrying a variable-length Answer-To-Reset (ATR) for card insertion or reset events.
Empty payload indicating a card has been removed from a reader on the client side.
Payload carrying a single APDU byte sequence in either direction. Variable-length data follows the struct.
Empty payload request from host to client asking for notification when all outstanding APDUs have been processed.
Empty payload sent by client to indicate completion of processing all outstanding APDUs in response to VSCMsgFlush.

functions.name: cac_card_init
functions.signature: VCardStatus cac_card_init(VReader *reader, VCard *card, unsigned char * const *cert, int cert_len[], VCardKey *key[], int cert_count);
functions.description: Initializes a CAC (Common Access Card) virtual card instance for use with a given virtual reader. The function binds certificate data and associated private keys to the VCard and prepares internal state so that CAC applets/commands can be served. Intended as the single public entry point for setting up the CAC card; typically called once during device/card initialization before any CAC operations are performed. Certificate buffers are provided as an array of pointers with corresponding lengths; keys are provided in a parallel array and are adopted (ownership transferred) by the card. Exact certificate encoding and key characteristics are not documented here; they are inferred to be certificate byte blobs and corresponding key objects used by the CAC emulation.
requirements: reader must be a valid, initialized VReader pointer (non-null).
card must be a valid VCard pointer (non-null) that can be initialized/configured by this call.
cert must be a valid pointer to an array of pointers to unsigned char; each cert[i] must reference at least cert_len[i] bytes valid for the duration of the call.
cert_len must point to an array with at least cert_count elements; each cert_len[i] must be >= 0 and correspond to cert[i].

key must point to an array with at least cert_count elements; each key[i] is a VCardKey* associated with cert[i]. The function adopts ownership of the provided keys (caller must not free them after a successful call).
cert_count must be >= 0 and represent the number of entries in cert/cert_len/key provided.
On return, the caller must check the VCardStatus result to determine success before using the configured card.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unspecified; avoid concurrent calls on the same card/reader unless the library documents it elsewhere.
Exact certificate formats (e.g., DER/BER/PKCS#7) and key types are unknown from this header and must match what the CAC implementation expects.

functions.name: vcard_response_new
functions.signature: VCardResponse *vcard_response_new(VCard *card, const unsigned char *buf, int len, int Le, vcard_7816_status_t status);
functions.description: Constructs a VCardResponse from an existing data buffer and a 7816 status code. Intended for creating an APDU response when you already have the response payload (buf/len) and a vcard_7816_status_t status, optionally honoring an ISO 7816 Le value.
requirements: card must point to a valid VCard instance (unknown ownership and lifetime expectations).
buf must be a valid pointer to at least len bytes when len > 0; may be NULL when len == 0.
len must be >= 0.
Le is an integer corresponding to ISO 7816 Le semantics; exact effect is unspecified in this header (unknown; not documented).
status must be a valid vcard_7816_status_t value.
On allocation failure this function may return NULL (not explicitly documented).

functions.name: vcard_response_new_bytes
functions.signature: VCardResponse *vcard_response_new_bytes(VCard *card, unsigned char *buf, int len, int Le, unsigned char sw1, unsigned char sw2);
functions.description: Constructs a VCardResponse from a data buffer and explicit SW1/SW2 status bytes. Use when you have the response payload and want to set the 7816 status bytes directly.
requirements: card must point to a valid VCard instance (unknown ownership and lifetime expectations).
buf must be a valid pointer to at least len bytes when len > 0; may be NULL when len == 0.
len must be >= 0.
Le is an integer corresponding to ISO 7816 Le semantics; exact effect is unspecified in this header (unknown; not documented).
sw1 and sw2 are 8-bit status bytes (no further restrictions documented).
On allocation failure this function may return NULL (not explicitly documented).
Ownership/aliasing of buf is unspecified by this header (unknown).

functions.name: vcard_response_new_status_bytes
functions.signature: VCardResponse *vcard_response_new_status_bytes(unsigned char sw1, unsigned char sw2);
functions.description: Constructs a VCardResponse that contains only status bytes (no data payload). Useful for signaling status-only responses.
requirements: sw1 and sw2 are 8-bit status bytes (no further restrictions documented).
Always ensure callers handle possible allocation failure; return value may be NULL (not explicitly documented).

functions.name: vcard_make_response
functions.description: Creates a VCardResponse from a vcard_7816_status_t status without a data payload. This call is guaranteed not to fail: if memory allocation is not possible, the returned response encodes VCARD7816_STATUS_EXC_ERROR_MEMORY_FAILURE.
requirements: status must be a valid vcard_7816_status_t value.
Caller may assume a non-NULL VCardResponse is always returned, per the note in the header.

functions.name: vcard_response_new_data
functions.description: Constructs a VCardResponse from a raw response buffer that already includes the encoded status bytes. Use when you have a complete APDU response (data + SW1/SW2) assembled.
requirements: buf must point to a buffer that already includes the status bytes encoded at the end of the response; format specifics are not documented here (inferred from comment).
len must be >= 0 and must reflect the size of buf; typical APDU responses include at least two status bytes (inferred; exact minimum not documented).
On allocation failure this function may return NULL (not explicitly documented).

functions.name: vcard_response_set_status_bytes
functions.signature: void vcard_response_set_status_bytes(VCardResponse *response, unsigned char sw1, unsigned char sw2);
functions.description: Sets the SW1 and SW2 status bytes on an existing VCardResponse.
requirements: response must be a valid, initialized VCardResponse pointer (must not be NULL).
sw1 and sw2 are 8-bit status bytes (no further restrictions documented).

functions.name: vcard_response_delete
functions.description: Destroys a VCardResponse and releases associated resources. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: May be called with response == NULL (explicitly documented).
After deletion, the response pointer becomes invalid; do not use it (standard destructor semantics).

functions.name: vcard_apdu_new
functions.signature: VCardAPDU *vcard_apdu_new(unsigned char *raw_apdu, int len, unsigned short *status);
functions.description: Parses or constructs a VCardAPDU from a raw APDU byte buffer. Intended as the entry point for converting incoming APDU bytes into an internal APDU object; a status code may be returned via the status pointer.
requirements: raw_apdu must be a valid pointer to at least len bytes when len > 0; may be NULL when len == 0 (not documented).
len must be >= 0 and should match the size of the APDU buffer provided; validity against ISO 7816 length rules is expected but not specified here (unknown).
status points to an unsigned short used to return a status/result of the APDU creation; whether this parameter is optional is not specified (unknown).
On allocation or parse failure this function may return NULL (not explicitly documented).

functions.name: vcard_apdu_delete
functions.description: Destroys a VCardAPDU and releases associated resources. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: May be called with apdu == NULL (explicitly documented).
After deletion, the apdu pointer becomes invalid; do not use it (standard destructor semantics).

functions.name: vcard_process_apdu
functions.description: Routes and processes an APDU against the specified virtual card. Always produces a valid response object via the response out-parameter.
requirements: card must point to a valid VCard instance ready for APDU processing (exact state requirements not documented).
apdu must be a valid VCardAPDU pointer representing the APDU to process.
response must be a non-NULL pointer to a VCardResponse* variable; on return it will point to a valid response (explicitly documented that it always returns a valid response).
Caller is responsible for eventually deleting the returned VCardResponse using vcard_response_delete (lifetime management inferred; not explicitly documented).
Function returns a VCardStatus indicating processing status; exact semantics of VCardStatus are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: vcard_emul_get_login_count
functions.description: Returns the number of remaining login attempts available on the emulated card. If the number is unknown, returns -1. Useful to enforce PIN retry policies or to inform users of remaining attempts.
requirements: card must be a valid, initialized VCard pointer
card must not be NULL
Callers must handle a return value of -1 as 'unknown' remaining attempts

functions.name: vcard_emul_login
functions.signature: vcard_7816_status_t vcard_emul_login(VCard *card, unsigned char *pin, int pin_len);
functions.description: Attempts to authenticate to the emulated card using the provided PIN. Returns a 7816 status word (sw2 || sw1) indicating success or the specific error per ISO 7816 semantics.
requirements: card must be a valid, initialized VCard pointer
card must not be NULL
pin must point to a buffer containing the PIN bytes
pin_len must be the length in bytes of the buffer pointed to by pin and must be non-negative
Callers must interpret the returned vcard_7816_status_t (SW) to determine success/failure

functions.name: vcard_emul_is_logged_in
functions.description: Reports whether the session is authenticated on the given emulated card. Returns a nonzero value if logged in, zero otherwise.
requirements: card must be a valid, initialized VCard pointer
card must not be NULL

functions.name: vcard_emul_logout
functions.description: Terminates the authenticated session on the emulated card, if any.
requirements: card must be a valid, initialized VCard pointer
card must not be NULL

functions.name: vcard_emul_delete_key
functions.description: Deletes/removes the specified key object from the emulated card or its key store.
requirements: key must be a valid VCardKey obtained from the emulator
key must not be NULL
After deletion, the key pointer must not be used again

functions.name: vcard_emul_rsa_bits
functions.description: Returns the RSA key size in bits for the provided key.
requirements: key must be a valid RSA VCardKey
key must not be NULL

functions.name: vcard_emul_rsa_op
functions.signature: vcard_7816_status_t vcard_emul_rsa_op(VCard *card, VCardKey *key, unsigned char *buffer, int buffer_size);
functions.description: Performs an RSA sign or decrypt operation using the provided key. The operation is done in-place on the supplied buffer. Returns an ISO 7816 status word indicating the result.
requirements: card must be a valid, initialized VCard pointer and must not be NULL
key must be a valid RSA VCardKey and must not be NULL
buffer must point to a writable memory region used both as input and output
buffer_size must be the size in bytes of buffer and must be non-negative
Callers must ensure buffer has sufficient size for the RSA operation; exact size requirements are unknown from this header
Callers must check the returned 7816 status word for success or error

functions.name: vcard_emul_reset
functions.description: Resets the emulated card with the specified power state transition (e.g., power on/off/cycle as defined by VCardPower).
requirements: card must be a valid, initialized VCard pointer
card must not be NULL
power must be a valid VCardPower value

functions.name: vcard_emul_get_atr
functions.description: Retrieves the card's ATR (Answer To Reset) bytes into the provided buffer and writes the ATR length to atr_len.
requirements: card must be a valid, initialized VCard pointer and must not be NULL
atr must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the ATR; exact maximum length is unknown from this header
atr_len must be a valid pointer to an int to receive the ATR length and must not be NULL

functions.name: vcard_emul_force_card_insert
functions.description: Simulates re-insertion of a card into the specified virtual reader, typically after a forced removal.
requirements: vreader must be a valid VReader pointer and must not be NULL
Caller must handle the returned VCardEmulError to determine success or failure

functions.name: vcard_emul_force_card_remove
functions.description: Forces a card removal event for the specified virtual reader even if the card is not physically removed.
requirements: vreader must be a valid VReader pointer and must not be NULL
Caller must handle the returned VCardEmulError to determine success or failure

functions.name: vcard_emul_options
functions.description: Parses emulator-specific option arguments and returns a VCardEmulOptions structure representing them. Use this to construct options prior to initializing the emulator.
requirements: args should be a NULL-terminated string of option arguments; exact format is emulator-specific and unknown from this header
Caller is responsible for managing the returned VCardEmulOptions per the library's ownership rules; exact lifetime management is unknown from this header
args may be NULL if supported; behavior for NULL is unknown from this header

functions.name: vcard_emul_init
functions.description: Initializes the emulator with the provided options. May return VCARD_EMUL_INIT_ALREADY_INITED if initialization has already occurred.
requirements: Must be called before using other emulator functions that require initialization
options must point to a valid options object created by vcard_emul_options (inferred) and may be NULL depending on implementation; exact NULL handling is unknown
Caller must check the returned VCardEmulError and handle VCARD_EMUL_INIT_ALREADY_INITED appropriately if re-initializing

functions.name: vcard_emul_finalize
functions.description: Finalizes and tears down the emulator, releasing resources allocated during initialization.
requirements: Should be called after vcard_emul_init to clean up resources
Should not be called concurrently with operations that assume the emulator is initialized (inferred)
Caller must check the returned VCardEmulError for success

functions.name: vcard_emul_replay_insertion_events
functions.description: Replays card insertion events, e.g., to notify listeners or resynchronize state after initialization or changes.
requirements: Should be called only when emulator state is valid/initialized; exact timing semantics are unknown from this header

functions.name: vcard_emul_usage
functions.description: Prints or displays usage information for emulator options and operation.
requirements: No explicit requirements; may produce output to stdout/stderr or a logging facility (unknown)

functions.name: vcard_emul_read_object
functions.signature: unsigned char *vcard_emul_read_object(VCard *card, const char *label, unsigned int *ret_len);
functions.description: Reads an object from the emulated card identified by label and returns a pointer to its byte contents, setting ret_len to the object length. Intended for retrieving stored data objects by name.
requirements: card must be a valid, initialized VCard pointer and must not be NULL
label must be a valid NULL-terminated string identifying the object and must not be NULL
ret_len must be a valid pointer to receive the length; behavior if NULL is unknown
Caller must manage the lifetime of the returned buffer per library ownership rules; exact ownership/cleanup requirements are unknown from this header

functions.name: vcard_init
functions.signature: VCardStatus vcard_init(VReader *vreader, VCard *vcard, VCardEmulType type, const char *params, unsigned char * const *cert, int cert_len[], VCardKey *key[], int cert_count);
functions.description: Initializes a virtual smart card instance for a given reader and emulation type. Intended to set up the VCard (vcard) using optional parameters and an optional set of certificates and keys. Typical usage: determine the emulation type, prepare or obtain any certificates/keys if needed, then call vcard_init and check the returned VCardStatus. Details about parameter format and certificate/key expectations are not documented here and may be emulator-specific.
requirements: vreader must reference a valid VReader object (in a state acceptable to the library for initialization).
vcard must point to a VCard object to be initialized; the object must be allocated by the caller.
type must be a valid member of VCardEmulType.
params may be NULL or a NUL-terminated string; exact accepted contents are emulator-specific and not documented here (unknown).
cert, cert_len, and key represent parallel arrays of length cert_count; if cert_count is 0, these may be NULL (inferred from signature).
For each i in [0, cert_count): cert[i] must point to a buffer containing a certificate (exact encoding unknown), and cert_len[i] must be the length in bytes of cert[i] and be non-negative.
For each i in [0, cert_count): key[i] must reference a VCardKey associated with the corresponding cert[i] (exact requirements unknown).
The caller must check the returned VCardStatus for success/failure; specific status codes are not documented here (unknown).
Memory ownership/lifetime of cert buffers and key objects during and after the call is not documented; callers should ensure they remain valid for at least the duration of the call (unknown).

functions.name: vcard_emul_type_select
functions.description: Selects the appropriate card emulation type for the given reader. Intended to be called to determine which VCardEmulType to use (e.g., before initializing a virtual card). Return value is one of the VCardEmulType enum values.
requirements: vreader must reference a valid VReader object.
Caller should handle any returned VCardEmulType value, including VCARD_EMUL_NONE, as a possible result (behavioral specifics for NONE are not documented).

functions.name: vcard_emul_type_from_string
functions.description: Parses a textual representation of an emulation type and returns the corresponding VCardEmulType. Useful for configuration-driven selection of the emulation type. Exact accepted strings and case-sensitivity are not documented here; callers should be prepared for unrecognized strings.
requirements: type_string must point to a NUL-terminated C string; behavior for NULL or empty strings is not documented (unknown).
Caller should handle any returned VCardEmulType value, including potentially VCARD_EMUL_NONE for unrecognized input (exact mapping and fallback behavior are not documented).

functions.name: vcard_buffer_response_new
functions.description: Create a response buffer object used to return data larger than a normal APDU response (nominally >254 bytes). Likely copies or references the provided data for segmented responses.
requirements: size must be >= 0.
If size > 0, buffer must point to at least size readable bytes.
Returned VCardBufferResponse* must be released with vcard_buffer_response_delete.

functions.name: vcard_buffer_response_delete
functions.description: Destroy a VCardBufferResponse previously created by vcard_buffer_response_new, releasing all associated resources.
requirements: buffer_response must be a valid pointer returned by vcard_buffer_response_new and not already deleted.
Do not use buffer_response after this call.

functions.name: vcard_reset
functions.description: Reset card state on a (power) reset event. Intended to reinitialize the card/applications according to the specified power state.
requirements: card must be a valid, initialized VCard pointer.
power must be a valid VCardPower enumeration value.

functions.name: vcard_new_applet
functions.signature: VCardApplet *vcard_new_applet(VCardProcessAPDU applet_process_function, VCardResetApplet applet_reset_function, const unsigned char *aid, int aid_len);
functions.description: Construct a VCardApplet with the given APDU processing function, reset callback, and Application Identifier (AID). Use to define a card applet that can be selected and process APDUs.
requirements: applet_process_function must be a valid function pointer implementing the applet's APDU handling.
If aid_len > 0, aid must point to at least aid_len bytes containing the applet AID.
aid_len must be >= 0.
Returned VCardApplet* should be destroyed with vcard_delete_applet when no longer needed.

functions.name: vcard_delete_applet
functions.description: Destroy a VCardApplet and free associated resources. Can safely be called with NULL.
requirements: May be called with applet == NULL (no effect).
If non-NULL, applet must be a valid pointer previously created by vcard_new_applet and not already deleted.
Do not use applet after this call.

functions.name: vcard_set_applet_private
functions.description: Associate card type–specific private data and an optional destructor with an applet.
requirements: applet must be non-NULL and valid.
_private may be NULL or a valid pointer to applet-specific data.
If provided, private_free must be a function compatible with the allocation of _private and will be used to free it.

functions.name: vcard_set_type
functions.description: Set the type of the VCard instance.
requirements: card must be non-NULL and valid.
type must be a valid VCardType value.

functions.name: vcard_add_applet
functions.description: Add a new applet to the given card so it can be found/selected and handle APDUs.

import random
import struct

# Target: generate a binary blob useful across stubs using FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME
# Strategy: emit a compact container holding multiple length-prefixed segments
# that the fuzzing stubs will slice for: certificates, response payloads, AIDs,
# serial numbers, APDU-like data, etc. All segments are valid byte strings.
#
# Layout (all little-endian):
#   magic 4B: b"VCBL" (Virtual Card Binary Layout)
#   version 1B: 1
#   counts 1B each: cert_count(0..3), has_payload(0/1), has_aid(0/1), has_serial(0/1)
#   reserved 1B: 0
#   For i in 0..cert_count-1: [u16 len][len bytes cert_i]
#   If has_payload: [u16 len][len bytes payload]
#   If has_aid:     [u8  len][len bytes aid]           (AID typically small)
#   If has_serial:  [u8  len][len bytes serial]
#   Tail optional extras to offer additional buffers for other stubs:
#      extra_count u8 (0..2)
#      extras: [u16 len][len bytes]
# Total capped to <= 4096 bytes.

ALPHABET_PRINT = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_"

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix printable and arbitrary bytes to cover varied consumers
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        mode = rng.randrange(4)
        if mode == 0:
            # printable run
            run = min(n - len(out), rng.randint(4, 32))
            for _ in range(run):
                out.append(ALPHABET_PRINT[rng.randrange(len(ALPHABET_PRINT))])
        elif mode == 1:
            # arbitrary bytes
            run = min(n - len(out), rng.randint(4, 32))
            out += rng.randbytes(run)
        elif mode == 2:
            # zero run
            run = min(n - len(out), rng.randint(2, 16))
            out += b"\x00" * run
        else:
            # structured mini-fields that look like DER-ish or APDU-ish
            run = min(n - len(out), rng.randint(6, 24))
            # simple TLV: tag, len, value
            t = rng.randrange(0x10, 0x7F)
            l = max(0, run - 2)
            out.append(t)
            out.append(l & 0xFF)
            if l:
                out += rng.randbytes(l)
    return bytes(out)

def _mk_cert(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Make a plausible certificate-like blob (not necessarily valid DER, but structured)
    # Size 64..512 as per stub bounds
    total = rng.randint(64, 512)
    # Start with a DER SEQUENCE header (0x30 len) with short or long form length
    body_len = total - 2
    if body_len < 0:
        body_len = 0
    if body_len < 128:
        hdr = bytes([0x30, body_len])
        remain = body_len
        payload = bytearray()
    else:
        # long form length up to 2 bytes
        l1 = body_len & 0xFF
        l2 = (body_len >> 8) & 0xFF
        hdr = bytes([0x30, 0x82, l2, l1])
        remain = total - len(hdr)
        payload = bytearray()
    # Fill with pseudo-TLV and random
    while remain > 0:
        chunk = min(remain, rng.randint(8, 64))
        payload += _rand_bytes(rng, chunk)
        remain -= chunk
    blob = hdr + bytes(payload)
    # Trim/pad to exact total
    if len(blob) > total:
        blob = blob[:total]
    elif len(blob) < total:
        blob += b"\x00" * (total - len(blob))
    return blob

def _mk_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # General response payload <= 1024
    return _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 1024))

def _mk_aid(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # AID length 5..16 typical; allow 0 to exercise empty path
    length = rng.choice([0] + list(range(5, 17)))
    if length == 0:
        return b""
    # ISO 7816 AIDs are binary; make mostly hex-like bytes with a fixed RID prefix sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.6 and length >= 5:
        # Common RID examples (randomly pick one)
        rid = rng.choice([
            b"\xA0\x00\x00\x00\x03",  # VISA
            b"\xA0\x00\x00\x00\x04",  # MasterCard
            b"\xA0\x00\x00\x00\x65",  # JCB
            b"\xA0\x00\x00\x00\x25",  # American Express
        ])
        rest = length - len(rid)
        return rid + _rand_bytes(rng, max(0, rest))
    else:
        return _rand_bytes(rng, length)

def _mk_serial(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Keep serial small (0..64) as per stub
    n = rng.randint(0, 64)
    if n == 0:
        return b""
    # Prefer printable for serials
    return bytes(ALPHABET_PRINT[rng.randrange(len(ALPHABET_PRINT))] for _ in range(n))

def _mk_extra(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Extra buffers for other consumers (e.g., xfr payloads)
    size = rng.randint(0, 256)
    return _rand_bytes(rng, size)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += b"VCBL"
    buf += b"\x01"  # version

    cert_count = rng.randint(0, 3)
    has_payload = 1 if rng.random() < 0.9 else 0
    has_aid = 1 if rng.random() < 0.9 else 0
    has_serial = 1 if rng.random() < 0.9 else 0

    buf += bytes([
        cert_count & 0xFF,
        has_payload & 0x01,
        has_aid & 0x01,
        has_serial & 0x01,
    ])
    buf += b"\x00"  # reserved/padding to keep simple alignment

    # Certificates
    for _ in range(cert_count):
        cert = _mk_cert(rng)
        # length prefix u16
        buf += struct.pack("<H", len(cert))
        buf += cert

    # Payload
    if has_payload:
        payload = _mk_payload(rng)
        if len(payload) > 1024:
            payload = payload[:1024]
        buf += struct.pack("<H", len(payload))
        buf += payload

    # AID
    if has_aid:
        aid = _mk_aid(rng)
        aid = aid[:16]

# Data type: APDU response bytes with trailing SW1/SW2
# Requirement: length >= 2, last two bytes are SW1 and SW2, preceding bytes (if any) are data.

    # Success
    (0x90, 0x00),  # OK
    # Warning
    (0x62, 0x00), (0x62, 0x81), (0x62, 0x82), (0x62, 0x83), (0x62, 0x84),

    x = max(0, min(0x0F, tries_left & 0x0F))
    return (0x63, 0xC0 | x)

# Generate a payload of target length with diverse patterns

def _gen_payload(rnd: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    if length <= 0:
        return b""
    # Occasionally use a canned payload truncated/extended
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        base = rnd.choice(_CANNED_PAYLOADS)
        if len(base) == length:
            return base
        elif len(base) > length:
            return base[:length]
        else:
            # Extend with pattern bytes
            pad_patterns = [b"\x00", b"\xFF", b"\xAA\x55", bytes(range(256))]
            pad = b""
            while len(base) + len(pad) < length:
                chunk = rnd.choice(pad_patterns)
                need = length - (len(base) + len(pad))
                pad += (chunk * (need // len(chunk) + 1))[:need]
            return base + pad
    # Otherwise compose patterns: segments of zeros, ff, ascending, random
    segments = []
    remain = length
    while remain > 0:
        seg_len = rnd.randint(1, min(64, remain))
        kind = rnd.random()
        if kind < 0.25:
            seg = bytes([0x00]) * seg_len
        elif kind < 0.5:
            seg = bytes([0xFF]) * seg_len
        elif kind < 0.75:
            start = rnd.randint(0, 255)
            seg = bytes((start + i) % 256 for i in range(seg_len))
        else:
            seg = bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(seg_len))

    return b"".join(segments)

    p = rnd.random()
    if p < 0.5:
        # Common predefined
        return rnd.choice(_SW_PAIRS_COMMON)
    elif p < 0.8:
        # PIN retry pattern 0..9 tries left
        return _pin_retry_sw(rnd.randint(0, 9))
    else:

        sw1_choices = [0x90, 0x62, 0x63, 0x67, 0x68, 0x69, 0x6A, 0x6C, 0x6D, 0x6E]
        sw1 = rnd.choice(sw1_choices)
        sw2 = rnd.getrandbits(8)

    payload_len = max(0, total_len - 2)

    sw1, sw2 = _choose_sw(rnd)

import random
from typing import List, Tuple

# ISO 7816 APDU builder
# Supports cases: Case 1 (no Lc/Le), Case 2s (Le), Case 3s (Lc+data), Case 4s (Lc+data+Le)
# and extended-length variants with 0x00 length field after header.

MAX_TOTAL = 1024  # fuzzer caps to 1024, stay within

ISO_INS_SET = [
    0xA4,  # SELECT
    0x20,  # VERIFY
    0x21,  # VERIFY (other)
    0x70,  # MANAGE CHANNEL
    0x84,  # GET CHALLENGE
    0x88,  # INTERNAL AUTHENTICATE
    0x82,  # EXTERNAL AUTHENTICATE
    0xB0,  # READ BINARY
    0xD6,  # UPDATE BINARY
    0xB2,  # READ RECORD
    0xE2,  # APP-specific / proprietary
    0x2A,  # PERFORM SECURITY OPERATION
]

# A few CLA values covering ISO/proprietary, secure messaging bits, and channels
CLA_POOL = [
    0x00,  # ISO interindustry
    0x80,  # proprietary
    0x94,  # channel encoded in lower bits
    0x0C,  # SM bit set in ISO CLA
    0x10,  # logical channel 1
    0x90,  # proprietary + channel
]

AID_SAMPLES = [
    bytes.fromhex("A000000003000000"),  # VISA
    bytes.fromhex("A0000000041010"),    # MasterCard
    bytes.fromhex("A000000308"),        # PIV
    bytes.fromhex("A0000000790100"),    # NIST SP 800-73 PIV AID variant
]

FILE_ID_SAMPLES = [b"3F00", b"2F00", b"5015", b"0001"]


def rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def pick_case(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Weight toward valid, diverse cases, include extended variants
    cases = [
        ("case1", 10),
        ("case2s", 15),
        ("case3s", 25),
        ("case4s", 25),
        ("case2e", 10),
        ("case3e", 10),
        ("case4e", 5),
    ]
    total = sum(w for _, w in cases)
    x = r.randrange(total)
    acc = 0
    for name, w in cases:
        acc += w
        if x < acc:
            return name
    return "case3s"


def cap_len(n: int) -> int:
    return max(0, min(n, MAX_TOTAL))


def build_header(r: random.Random) -> Tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    cla = r.choice(CLA_POOL)
    ins = r.choice(ISO_INS_SET)
    p1 = r.randrange(0, 256)
    p2 = r.randrange(0, 256)
    return cla, ins, p1, p2


def build_select_data(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Sometimes build P1/P2 accordingly outside; data here is AID or name
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        aid = r.choice(AID_SAMPLES)
        # Occasionally append path or extra bytes
        if r.random() < 0.2:
            aid += rand_bytes(r, r.randrange(1, 5))
        return aid
    else:
        # File name/path
        name = r.choice(FILE_ID_SAMPLES)
        return bytes.fromhex(name.decode())


def normalize_len_short(n: int) -> int:
    # Lc/Le short fit in 1 byte; 0 encodes 256 for Le in short case
    return n & 0xFF


def encode_short_case(lc: int = None, data: bytes = b"", le: int = None) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    if lc is not None:
        out.append(normalize_len_short(lc))
        out += data[: lc & 0xFF]
    if le is not None:
        out.append(normalize_len_short(le if le != 256 else 0))
    return bytes(out)


def encode_extended_case(lc: int = None, data: bytes = b"", le: int = None) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    out.append(0x00)
    if lc is not None:
        out += bytes([(lc >> 8) & 0xFF, lc & 0xFF])
        out += data[:lc]
    if le is not None:
        out += bytes([(le >> 8) & 0xFF, le & 0xFF])
    return bytes(out)


def limit_lengths_for_total(base_len: int, want_lc: int, want_le: int, extended: bool) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    # Compute maximum payload allowed so total <= MAX_TOTAL
    overhead = base_len
    if extended:
        overhead += 1  # leading 0x00
        if want_lc is not None:
            overhead += 2
        if want_le is not None:
            overhead += 2
    else:
        if want_lc is not None:
            overhead += 1
        if want_le is not None:
            overhead += 1
    remaining = max(0, MAX_TOTAL - overhead)
    lc = min(want_lc or 0, remaining)
    if want_lc is not None:
        remaining -= lc
    le = min(want_le or 0, remaining)
    return lc, le


def build_apdu(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    cla, ins, p1, p2 = build_header(r)
    case = pick_case(r)

    # Specialize some instructions for realistic parameters
    data_bytes = b""
    desired_lc = None
    desired_le = None

    if ins == 0xA4:  # SELECT
        # P1 selects by AID 0x04 or by name 0x08; P2 first/next
        p1 = r.choice([0x04, 0x08, 0x00])
        p2 = r.choice([0x00, 0x04, 0x0C])
        if case in ("case3s", "case4s", "case3e", "case4e"):
            data_bytes = build_select_data(r)
            desired_lc = len(data_bytes)
        if case in ("case2s", "case4s", "case2e", "case4e"):
            desired_le = r.choice([0, 1, 2, 0x10, 0x100, 256])

    elif ins in (0xB0, 0xB2):  # READ BINARY/RECORD
        # p1/p2 as offsets/record/short EF id
        if ins == 0xB0:
            # offset high/low
            p1 = r.randrange(0, 0x80)  # no EF select by short id
            p2 = r.randrange(0, 256)
        else:  # READ RECORD
            p1 = r.randrange(1, 0xFE)
            p2 = r.choice([0x04, 0x00, 0x02])
        desired_le = r.choice([0, 0x10, 0xFF, 256])
        case = "case2s" if "e" not in case else "case2e"

    elif ins in (0xD6,):  # UPDATE BINARY
        # Build some data
        data_len = r.randrange(1, 64)
        data_bytes = rand_bytes(r, data_len)
        desired_lc = len(data_bytes)
        # p1/p2 as offset
        p1 = r.randrange(0, 0x80)
        p2 = r.randrange(0, 256)
        case = "case3s" if r.random() < 0.8 else "case3e"

    elif ins in (0x2A, 0x88, 0x82):  # PSO / AUTH
        # make plausible crypto payload sizes
        k = r.choice([8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256])
        data_bytes = rand_bytes(r, k)
        desired_lc = len(data_bytes)
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            desired_le = r.choice([0, 16, 32, 256])
            case = "case4s" if r.random() < 0.7 else "case4e"
        else:
            case = "case3s" if r.random() < 0.7 else "case3e"

    else:
        # Generic behavior
        if case in ("case3s", "case4s", "case3e", "case4e"):
            desired_lc = r.randrange(0, 300) if "e" in case else r.randrange(0, 255)
            data_bytes = rand_bytes(r, desired_lc)
        if case in ("case2s", "case4s", "case2e", "case4e"):
            desired_le = r.choice([0, r.randrange(1, 255), 256, r.randrange(257, 1024)])

    header = bytes([cla, ins, p1, p2])

    # Fit within limits
    extended = case.endswith("e")
    lc_adj, le_adj = limit_lengths_for_total(4, desired_lc, desired_le, extended)

    if extended:
        body = encode_extended_case(lc_adj if desired_lc is not None else None,
                                    data_bytes,
                                    le_adj if desired_le is not None else None)
    else:
        # For short Le, encode 0 as 0x00 meaning 256 when Le present
        le_short = None
        if desired_le is not None:
            if le_adj == 256:
                le_short = 0
            else:
                le_short = max(0, min(le_adj, 255))
        lc_short = None if desired_lc is None else max(0, min(lc_adj, 255))
        body = encode_short_case(lc_short, data_bytes, le_short)

    apdu = header + body
    return apdu[:MAX_TOTAL]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Mix deterministic seed with slight variability while staying deterministic per seed
    # Use multiple tries to cover different cases depending on seed value
    apdu = build_apdu(r)
    # Ensure occasionally zero-length APDU to exercise parser edge
    if len(apdu) == 0 or (seed % 17 == 0 and len(apdu) > 5):
        # produce a valid minimal Case 1 or empty buffer
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            apdu = bytes([r.choice(CLA_POOL), r.choice(ISO_INS_SET), 0x00, 0x00])
        else:
            apdu = b""  # some implementations accept len==0 path per docs
    return bytes(apdu)

import random
from typing import List

# Data type: PIN bytes
# - Short byte string representing a PIN value
# - In this fuzzing stub, pin length is taken as (len(input) % 17), so any input
#   yields an effective PIN length in the range 0..16.
# - The buffer provided by FUZZ_PARAM_STR() is used as the source of bytes.
# Strategy:
# - Generate seeded, interesting byte sequences whose lengths exercise different
#   modulo 17 results (0..16). We pack multiple PIN candidates into one buffer
#   separated by a delimiter so the fuzzer can choose among them by slicing.
# - Cover common PIN patterns (numeric ASCII), boundary lengths (0,1,2,3,7,8,9,15,16),
#   repeated digits, increasing/decreasing sequences, high-bytes, zero bytes, and random bytes.
# - Keep total output <= 4096 bytes.

DELIM = b"\n--PIN--\n"


def _numeric_ascii(n: int) -> bytes:
    # Repeat decimal digits to reach length n
    s = ("0123456789" * ((n + 9)//10))[:n]
    return s.encode()


def _repeat_byte(b: int, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([b]) * n


def _seq_up(n: int, start: int = 0) -> bytes:
    return bytes((start + i) % 256 for i in range(n))


def _seq_down(n: int, start: int = 255) -> bytes:
    return bytes((start - i) % 256 for i in range(n))


def _hex_ascii(n: int) -> bytes:
    s = ("0123456789ABCDEF" * ((n + 15)//16))[:n]
    return s.encode()


def _rng_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _mix_patterns(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix digits, zeros, high bytes
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    k = max(1, n // 3)
    parts.append(_numeric_ascii(min(k, n)))
    rem = n - len(parts[-1])
    if rem > 0:
        parts.append(_repeat_byte(0x00, min(k, rem)))
        rem = n - sum(len(p) for p in parts)
    if rem > 0:
        parts.append(_repeat_byte(0xFF, rem))
    mixed = b"".join(parts)
    # Randomly shuffle segments with a small probability
    if r.random() < 0.3 and len(mixed) > 0:
        lst = list(mixed)
        r.shuffle(lst)
        mixed = bytes(lst)
    return mixed


def _build_candidates(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Target effective lengths 0..16 due to modulo behavior
    targets = list(range(0, 17))
    r.shuffle(targets)

    candidates: List[bytes] = []

    # Ensure we include boundary and common PINs explicitly
    boundary = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 15, 16]
    for n in boundary:
        # Multiple variants per length to explore content diversity
        variants: List[bytes] = []
        if n == 0:
            variants.append(b"")
        else:
            variants.extend([
                _numeric_ascii(n),
                _repeat_byte(0x00, n),
                _repeat_byte(0xFF, n),
                _seq_up(n, start=r.randrange(0, 256)),
                _seq_down(n, start=r.randrange(0, 256)),
                _hex_ascii(n),
                _mix_patterns(r, n),
                _rng_bytes(r, n),
            ])
        # Choose a couple based on randomness to stay compact
        pick = 2 if n > 0 else 1
        r.shuffle(variants)
        candidates.extend(variants[:pick])

    # Add some random-length candidates to cover remaining modulo classes
    for _ in range(10):
        # produce lengths that map to different (len % 17)
        base = r.randrange(0, 17)
        # optionally add full 17-blocks to alter raw length but keep same modulo
        extra_blocks = r.randrange(0, 3)
        n = base + 17 * extra_blocks
        if n == 0:
            candidates.append(b"")
        else:
            choice = r.random()
            if choice < 0.2:
                candidates.append(_numeric_ascii(n))
            elif choice < 0.4:
                candidates.append(_rng_bytes(r, n))
            elif choice < 0.6:
                candidates.append(_mix_patterns(r, n))
            elif choice < 0.8:
                candidates.append(_seq_up(n, start=r.randrange(0, 256)))
            else:
                candidates.append(_seq_down(n, start=r.randrange(0, 256)))

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    unique: List[bytes] = []
    for c in candidates:
        key = (len(c), c[:32])  # cheap key
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        unique.append(c)

    return unique


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a palette of PIN candidates
    candidates = _build_candidates(r)

    # Optionally rotate order to vary first candidate (important because many fuzzers
    # prefer early bytes). This is still deterministic by seed.
    if candidates:
        rot = r.randrange(0, len(candidates))
        candidates = candidates[rot:] + candidates[:rot]

    # Join with delimiter so FUZZ_PARAM_STR() can read any slice/substring
    buf = DELIM.join(candidates)

    # Ensure we do not exceed 4096 bytes; if larger, truncate at delimiter boundary
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        # Try to cut at the last delimiter before the limit
        cut = buf.rfind(DELIM, 0, 4096)
        if cut == -1:
            buf = buf[:4096]
        else:
            buf = buf[:cut]

    return bytes(buf)

import string
from typing import List

# Data type: identifier string
# Used by stubs:
# - vcard_emul_read_object: label string (<=128 bytes when passed through FUZZ_PARAM_STR())
# - vcard_emul_type_from_string: type string parsed into enum {none,cac,passthru}
# - vreader_new: reader name string (<=128 bytes)
# - vreader_get_reader_by_name: lookup name string (<=128 bytes)
# The generator should return a single bytes buffer that FUZZ framework will slice to serve
# successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls. We therefore pack multiple interesting, NUL-terminated
# strings back-to-back. Each is crafted to be valid and to exercise different code paths.

# Strategy:
# 1) Include canonical known identifiers expected by vcard_emul_type_from_string:
#    "none", "NONE", "cac", "CAC", "passthru", "PASSTHRU" and some variants.
# 2) Include plausible reader names typical in systems: "Reader 0", "Virtual Reader", etc.
# 3) Include plausible object labels used by CAC/vcard emulators (common file/object names):
#    "CAC.CERT.PKI", "CERT1", "PKI_CERT", "PIV.AUTH", etc.
# 4) Add edge cases: empty string, 1-char, max-length 128, strings with spaces, unicode bytes,
#    and strings with embedded punctuation.
# 5) All strings are NUL-terminated; the combined buffer stays <= 4096 bytes.


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return rng.choice(items)


def _make_known_type_strings() -> List[str]:
    variants = [
        "none", "NONE", "None",
        "cac", "CAC", "CaC",
        "passthru", "PASSTHRU", "PassThru", "pass-through", "pass_thru",
    ]
    return variants


def _make_reader_names() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "Virtual Reader", "Reader 0", "Reader-1", "USB SmartCard Reader",
        "PCSC Reader", "Emulated Reader", "Test Reader A", "My Reader",
        "Workstation-Reader", "SmartCard Interface",
    ]


def _make_labels() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "CAC.CERT.PKI", "CERT1", "CERT2", "PKI_CERT", "PIV.AUTH", "PIV.SIGN",
        "OBJECT1", "KEY_MGMT", "CHUID", "FASC-N", "DISCOVERY_OBJECT",
        "CardCapabilityContainer", "SecurityObject", "CardHolderUniqueID",
    ]


def _random_identifier(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 128) -> str:
    # Mix letters, digits, space, dash, underscore, dot
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " -_.:/"
    n = rng.randint(0, max_len)  # allow empty as edge case
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _random_unicode_like(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> bytes:
    # Generate bytes that look like UTF-8: choose from valid ASCII plus some multi-byte sequences
    out = bytearray()
    target = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    while len(out) < target:
        t = rng.random()
        if t < 0.7:
            out.append(rng.randint(0x20, 0x7E))
        elif t < 0.85:
            # 2-byte UTF-8
            cp = rng.randint(0x00A0, 0x07FF)
            out.append(0xC0 | (cp >> 6))
            out.append(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F))
        elif t < 0.95:
            # 3-byte UTF-8
            cp = rng.randint(0x0800, 0xFFFF)
            out.append(0xE0 | (cp >> 12))
            out.append(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F))
            out.append(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F))
        else:
            # punctuation burst
            for ch in ",.;+-_=()[]{}@#%&!":
                out.append(ord(ch))
    return bytes(out[:max_len])


def _nul(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Ensure single NUL terminator
    return s + b"\x00"


def _to_bytes(s: str) -> bytes:
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Known type strings (ensure these appear early for vcard_emul_type_from_string)
    types = _make_known_type_strings()
    rng.shuffle(types)
    for t in types[:rng.randint(3, len(types))]:
        parts.append(_nul(_to_bytes(t)))

    # 2) Reader names: mix known and random
    readers = _make_reader_names()
    rng.shuffle(readers)
    for r in readers[:rng.randint(3, len(readers))]:
        # Limit to 128 as per stub constraint
        rs = r[:128]
        parts.append(_nul(_to_bytes(rs)))
    # Add some random reader-like identifiers
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        rid = _random_identifier(rng, 128)
        parts.append(_nul(_to_bytes(rid)))

    # 3) Labels for vcard_emul_read_object: include known and random
    labels = _make_labels()
    rng.shuffle(labels)
    for l in labels[:rng.randint(4, len(labels))]:
        parts.append(_nul(_to_bytes(l[:128])))
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        # Construct hierarchical labels like "PIV.OBJECT/NAME-123"
        base = _rand_choice(rng, ["PIV", "CAC", "OBJ", "FILE", "DATA", "KEY"]) \
               + _rand_choice(rng, [".", "/", ":"]) \
               + _random_identifier(rng, 20)
        parts.append(_nul(_to_bytes(base[:128])))

    # 4) Edge cases
    parts.append(b"\x00")  # empty string
    parts.append(_nul(b"a"))
    parts.append(_nul(b" "))
    parts.append(_nul(_to_bytes("none\x00none")))  # includes internal NUL when read whole; FUZZ uses c_str up to first NUL
    # Max-length string (128 chars)
    max_str = "X" * 128
    parts.append(_nul(_to_bytes(max_str)))
    # Unicode-like bytes
    parts.append(_nul(_random_unicode_like(rng, 64)))

    # Shuffle segments to vary order while keeping early type strings already added beneficial
    middle = parts[1:]
    rng.shuffle(middle)
    parts = [parts[0]] + middle  # keep the very first item as a known type string

    # Concatenate and ensure size limit
    buf = b"".join(parts)
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4095] + b"\x00"  # keep final as NUL-terminated boundary

    return buf
